heroHeadline: SAF Government Returns to Khartoum; EU Sanctions Both Sides; SAF Strikes Hemedti's Hometown Al Zorg, Killing 64 Civilians
heroSubtitle: On Day 1125, Sudan's SAF-aligned government formally announced its complete return to Khartoum from Port Sudan, ending a 25-month wartime displacement — the Central Bank of Sudan also resumed capital operations for the first time since April 2023. The EU imposed targeted sanctions on seven Sudan conflict principals, including Hemedti's brother Major Algoney Hamdan Dagalo Musa (RSF) and SAF-allied Al-Bara' ibn Malik Battalion commander Al-Misbah Abu Zaid Talha — marking the first time a major international actor simultaneously sanctioned individuals from both warring sides. SAF airstrikes on Al Zorg, Hemedti's North Darfur hometown and tribal heartland, killed at least 64 civilians, destroyed the local hospital, and killed two of Hemedti's relatives and tribal leader Bashir Barma Baraka Allah — one of the war's most symbolically charged strikes. These developments come as the war enters its fourth year: RSF retains all five Darfur state capitals but faces growing command fractures — Brigadier General El Safana's May 11 defection is the third senior RSF departure in two months, and analysts at Asharq Al-Awsat assess a potential RSF 'breakup phase.' Sudan remains the world's largest humanitarian crisis: 14 million displaced, 19.1 million at IPC3+ acute food insecurity, famine confirmed in El Fasher and Kadugli, and the UN 2026 appeal only 16% funded.
